environment: Node executing actual sql.js WebAssembly, presentation SQLite adapter and academy service. Structured-cloned memory persistence simulates IndexedDB snapshots; every request reconstructs SQLite from persisted bytes.
scope: Public synthetic demonstration; role checks validate application behavior and are not a security boundary in a client-side application.

checks.name: Source invariants: 14 areas, 42 original performance fields, 24 unanswered requirements
Browser-local launcher accepts a Request without a network Origin header
Browser-local session header opens the selected account and rejects malformed tokens
SQLite WASM seed and role launcher persist 30 synthetic learners
Role rules reject wrong-role and unassigned requests in the demo logic
D01 explanation and draft survive logout, relogin and engine recreation
D01 duplicate submission creates one attempt and one reward
Instructor return, learner correction, acceptance, portfolio and IVP complete the loop
36 lessons and 108 questions preserve content and six checkpoint links
Quiz gives explained correction and awards points once across repeated attempts
Lesson work is durable, editable, exported and rewarded only once
Attachment bytes survive engine recreation and follow demo ownership rules
Storage failure never reports success and retries preserve one durable operation
Storage failure atomically discards both new attachment and its record
Persisted SQLite snapshot is consistent and contains no practical qualification

limitations: Native browser IndexedDB, Web Locks and quota behavior are not exercised by this Node test.
DOM rendering, mobile layout, navigation, downloads and deployed GitHub Pages require separate browser checks.
Cross-device shared storage and secure real-user authentication are intentionally outside this presentation.
